doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Kenny Clarke and the first bebop drumming
summary: Klook was the first bebop drummer he heard, keeping time on the right hand and dropping the four-beat bass drum.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: You mention Diz and Bird, but you don’t mention the drummers they were playing with. Was it the overall music that got you, and not necessarily the drumming?
Both. Overall music and the drumming too, because Kenny – you know who I’m talking about.

Kenny Clarke – Klook – was the first guy I heard that played what you call bebop drums. He didn’t need a left hand or right foot. It was all here in the right hand. When the syncopation came in with the bass drum, he had it all in the right place. He didn’t have to go boom-boom-boom-boom-boom like we had to do in the swing bands, because the bass player played that. Ray Brown gives you four beats. You didn’t need anything more after that.
